blocks.content: Tides and waves are two important types of oceanic movements. While waves are primarily generated by wind and affect only the surface layer of water, tides are large-scale periodic rise and fall of sea level caused by gravitational forces of the Moon and the Sun. Both play a critical role in coastal processes, navigation, fisheries, and climate interaction.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Waves represent the movement of energy across the ocean surface, while individual water particles move in small circular orbits.
Tides are the periodic rise and fall of sea levels caused by the gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun, combined with Earth's centrifugal force.
Spring tides occur during New Moon and Full Moon phases when the Sun, Earth, and Moon are aligned in a straight line (Syzygy).
Neap tides occur during the First and Third Quarter moon phases when the Sun and Moon form a right angle relative to Earth (Quadrature).
Tides play a crucial role in desilting estuaries, aiding navigation in shallow harbors, and generating clean tidal power.

blocks.content: Ocean waves are oscillatory movements of water particles caused mainly by wind energy transferred to the ocean surface. In waves, water particles move in circular motion but the water itself does not travel long distances.
• Generated mainly by wind speed, duration, and fetch (distance over which wind blows).
• Energy moves forward but water particles move in circular paths.
• Tsunamis are seismic waves, not wind-generated waves.

blocks.content: • Wind Waves – Generated by surface winds.
• Storm Waves – Higher waves during cyclones.
• Tsunami – Caused by earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, or landslides.
• Tidal Waves – Misleading term; actual tides are gravitational.
Tides are the periodical rise and fall of the sea level, once or twice a day, mainly due to the attraction of the sun and the moon.

Tides are the periodic rise and fall of ocean water levels caused primarily by the gravitational pull of the Moon and secondarily by the Sun. The Moon exerts a stronger tidal force due to its proximity to Earth.
• High tide – When sea level rises.
• Low tide – When sea level falls.
• Occurs twice daily in most coastal areas.
• Centrifugal force due to Earth-Moon rotation also contributes.

On the side of Earth facing the Moon, gravitational pull causes water to bulge outward (high tide). On the opposite side, centrifugal force creates another bulge. Areas between these bulges experience low tide.

blocks.content: • Help in navigation and port operations.

items: Syzygy refers to the straight-line alignment of the Sun, Earth, and Moon causing maximum tidal range (Spring Tides).
Quadrature occurs when the Sun and Moon are at a 90-degree angle to Earth, creating minimum tidal range (Neap Tides).
The time interval between two consecutive high tides is 12 hours and 25 minutes due to the Moon's orbital progression around Earth.
Tidal rivers like the Hooghly in India depend on high tides for ocean-going vessels to enter the port safely.

blocks.content:
• Tides are caused mainly by Moon's gravitational pull.

• Spring tides occur during full and new moon.

• Neap tides occur during first and third quarter.

• Tsunami is a seismic sea wave.

• Semi-diurnal tides are most common globally.
